rows.label: Points scored per game vs points allowed per game, all 32 clubs
rows.note: Both sides official and recomputed from the same 32 rows. The sign here is a fact about this 2026 sample, not about strategy: a negative value means high-scoring clubs have tended to concede less, a positive one the opposite. Neither is an edge.

rows.label: Win differential vs point differential, all 32 clubs
rows.note: Control row: this must be high, and it is. If it were not, the transcription would be wrong. It is a data-integrity check dressed as a correlation.

rows.label: Own spread line vs actual home margin (this namespace's model)
rows.note: NOT COMPUTED. The own model is available for all 14 week-10 games but only one of those games has been played, so n = 1 at best and a correlation is meaningless. Left blank on purpose; the number appears when the games finish.

rows.label: Same-game dependence: home covers AND game goes over
rows.note: The prior session reports r = 0.0083 on n = 3,912 games from the third-party archive. That archive is third-party, so under this namespace's rule the value is NOT republished as ours: it is cited, with its n, as someone else's number resting on a source this namespace does not treat as official. Reproducing it needs official prices we do not have.

rule: Only values that both sides of the correlation can be sourced for are computed. Each row names which side is official and which is third-party. A row where either side is missing is printed blank with the reason, never filled in. n is published on every row, always.
